feed.title: Clausery: guides and clause library
feed.subtitle: Practical guides to drafting and automating documents, and plain-English explanations of contract clauses.

entry.title: What to include in an NDA: a clause-by-clause checklist
entry.summary: The clauses a non-disclosure agreement needs, from the definition of confidential information to exclusions, term, return of information and governing law, and when to use a mutual or one-way NDA.

entry.title: What to include in a statement of work (SOW)
entry.summary: The sections every statement of work needs: scope, deliverables, timeline, fees, assumptions, acceptance and change control, with examples of what goes wrong when they are missing.

entry.title: Repeating lists and table rows in Word templates
entry.summary: How to make a Word template repeat a paragraph, bullet or table row for every party, attorney, deliverable or line item, with separators and numbering.

entry.title: Mail merge vs document automation: which one do you need?
entry.summary: Mail merge fills the same blanks from a spreadsheet; document automation also includes or removes clauses, repeats lists and calculates. How to tell which one your documents need.

entry.title: How to write a job offer letter (with a free template)
entry.summary: What to put in a job offer letter: role, start date, pay, bonus, equity, benefits, conditions and at-will wording, plus the mistakes that cause disputes later.

entry.title: How to write a demand letter for unpaid invoices
entry.summary: A step-by-step guide to asking a customer for overdue payment in writing: what to include, tone, deadlines, interest, and what to do if they still do not pay.

entry.title: Choosing document software when client confidentiality matters: a checklist
entry.summary: Questions to ask before putting client or employee information into any document or drafting tool: where data is processed, who can access it, sub-processors, retention and exit.

entry.title: Conditional clauses in Word: include or remove paragraphs automatically
entry.summary: How to make parts of a Word document appear only when they apply: yes/no sections, either/or wording, clauses based on amounts or dates, and removing empty lines.

entry.title: Client intake without a portal: collect answers by email, privately
entry.summary: How to send clients a questionnaire they can fill in offline and return as a file, so you can generate documents from their answers without a client portal or account.

entry.title: How to automate a Word template without uploading it anywhere
entry.summary: A step-by-step guide to turning any Word document into a reusable, fill-in-the-blanks template with questions, conditional clauses and lists, entirely in your browser.

entry.title: Warranty clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A warranty is a contractual promise about a fact or about quality, such as that services will be performed with reasonable skill and care, or that software will work as specified for 90 days. Free sample warranty clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Waiver clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A no-waiver clause says that if a party does not enforce a right straight away, for example by accepting a late payment without complaint, it has not given that right up. Free sample waiver clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Termination for convenience clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A termination for convenience clause lets a party end the contract without giving any reason, usually on a period of written notice. Free sample termination for convenience clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Termination for cause clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A termination for cause clause lets a party end the contract when the other party commits a material breach and does not fix it in time, or becomes insolvent. Free sample termination for cause clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Survival clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A survival clause lists the obligations that continue after a contract ends, such as confidentiality, payment, indemnities and limits on liability. Free sample survival clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Severability clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A severability clause says that if one part of the contract is invalid or unenforceable, the rest of the contract still stands, and the invalid part is trimmed or removed. Free sample severability clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Payment terms clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: The payment terms clause says when a party can invoice, how long the other party has to pay, in what currency and by what method, and what happens when an invoice is disputed. Free sample payment terms clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Notices clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A notices clause says how formal notices under the contract, such as notices of breach, renewal or termination, must be sent, to which address, and when they count as received. Free sample notices clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Non-solicitation clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A non-solicitation clause stops a party from actively approaching the other party's employees, contractors or customers for a period, usually during the contract and for a time after it ends. Free sample non-solicitation clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Non-compete clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A non-compete clause prevents a person or business from working for, or running, a competing business for a period and within an area after a relationship ends. Free sample non-compete clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Limitation of liability clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A limitation of liability clause caps how much one party can recover from the other, and usually excludes whole categories of loss, such as lost profits and indirect or consequential damages. Free sample limitation of liability clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Late payment interest clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A late payment clause lets the party that is owed money charge interest on overdue amounts, and often suspend work until it is paid. Free sample late payment interest clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Intellectual property assignment clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: An intellectual property clause decides who owns the copyright, designs, inventions and other rights in the work created under a contract, and what each side may do with the other's pre-existing material. Free sample intellectual property assignment clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Independent contractor clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: This clause records that a person is engaged as an independent business, not as an employee, and that they are responsible for their own taxes, insurance and working arrangements. Free sample independent contractor clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Indemnification clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: An indemnity is a promise by one party to cover the other party's losses if a specified kind of claim arises, most often a claim by a third party caused by the first party's breach, negligence or infringement of someone else's intellectual property. Free sample indemnification clause wording, what t

entry.title: Governing law and jurisdiction clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A governing law clause chooses which country's or state's law applies to the contract. Free sample governing law and jurisdiction clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Force majeure clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A force majeure clause excuses a party from performing, for as long as an extraordinary event outside its control prevents it: natural disasters, war, epidemics, government orders and similar events. Free sample force majeure clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Entire agreement clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: An entire agreement clause, also called an integration or merger clause, says that the written contract contains everything the parties agreed, replacing earlier emails, proposals and conversations. Free sample entire agreement clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Counterparts and electronic signature clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A counterparts clause lets each party sign a separate copy of the contract, with all copies together forming one agreement. Free sample counterparts and electronic signature clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Dispute resolution clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A dispute resolution clause sets out the steps the parties must take when they disagree: usually negotiation between senior people first, then mediation, then arbitration or court. Free sample dispute resolution clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Confidentiality clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: A confidentiality clause obliges a party to keep the other party's non-public information secret, use it only for the purpose of the contract, and share it only with people who need to know it. Free sample confidentiality clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: At-will employment clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: An at-will clause states that either the employer or the employee can end the employment at any time, with or without cause or notice, as US law generally allows. Free sample at-will employment clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Assignment clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: An assignment clause says whether a party can transfer its rights under the contract to someone else, for example when it sells its business, and on what conditions. Free sample assignment clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.

entry.title: Amendment clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: An amendment or variation clause says how the contract can be changed, usually only by a written document signed by both parties. Free sample amendment clause wording, what to check, and FAQs.
